title: Interactive Maps
text:
CALIFORNIA · OFFICIAL COUNTY DATA



Explore certified results from the June 2026 gubernatorial primary, primary turnout, and the 2024 presidential vote. Hover over a county for the details behind each shade.



58

California countiesThree interactive views

OFFICIAL RETURNS







01 · CERTIFIED RESULTS



County colors show the party of the leading candidate in California’s June 2, 2026 gubernatorial primary. Hover to see the county leader, runner-up, votes, and each candidate’s share of all votes cast in the county contest.




Input to asJSON(keep_vec_names=TRUE) is a named vector. In a future version of jsonlite, this option will not be supported, and named vectors will be translated into arrays instead of objects. If you want JSON object output, please use a named list instead. See ?toJSON.
Input to asJSON(keep_vec_names=TRUE) is a named vector. In a future version of jsonlite, this option will not be supported, and named vectors will be translated into arrays instead of objects. If you want JSON object output, please use a named list instead. See ?toJSON.
Input to asJSON(keep_vec_names=TRUE) is a named vector. In a future version of jsonlite, this option will not be supported, and named vectors will be translated into arrays instead of objects. If you want JSON object output, please use a named list instead. See ?toJSON.
Input to asJSON(keep_vec_names=TRUE) is a named vector. In a future version of jsonlite, this option will not be supported, and named vectors will be translated into arrays instead of objects. If you want JSON object output, please use a named list instead. See ?toJSON.







How to read it. California’s top-two primary includes candidates from all parties. This map identifies the highest-vote candidate within each county; it does not show the statewide top two or imply a general-election winner.


Sources: California Secretary of State, June 2, 2026 Statement of Vote, Governor by County (XLSX); county boundaries: U.S. Census Bureau, 2024 TIGER/Line County shapefile.








02 · VOTER PARTICIPATION



Blue shading shows June 2026 primary turnout for each county. Hover for the percentage and its official ballot and registration counts.




Input to asJSON(keep_vec_names=TRUE) is a named vector. In a future version of jsonlite, this option will not be supported, and named vectors will be translated into arrays instead of objects. If you want JSON object output, please use a named list instead. See ?toJSON.
Input to asJSON(keep_vec_names=TRUE) is a named vector. In a future version of jsonlite, this option will not be supported, and named vectors will be translated into arrays instead of objects. If you want JSON object output, please use a named list instead. See ?toJSON.
Input to asJSON(keep_vec_names=TRUE) is a named vector. In a future version of jsonlite, this option will not be supported, and named vectors will be translated into arrays instead of objects. If you want JSON object output, please use a named list instead. See ?toJSON.
Input to asJSON(keep_vec_names=TRUE) is a named vector. In a future version of jsonlite, this option will not be supported, and named vectors will be translated into arrays instead of objects. If you want JSON object output, please use a named list instead. See ?toJSON.







How it is calculated. Turnout is ballots cast divided by registered voters, using the Secretary of State’s county participation table. Its registered-voter denominator is based on the 15-day registration report; the state’s footnote notes that same-day registration can occur through Election Day.


Source: California Secretary of State, June 2, 2026 Statement of Vote, Voter Participation Statistics by County. County boundaries: U.S. Census Bureau, 2024 TIGER/Line County shapefile.








03 · HISTORICAL GENERAL ELECTION



The red-to-blue scale shows the two-party margin between Kamala Harris and Donald Trump in the November 5, 2024 general election. Near-neutral counties were more competitive; zoom or hover for both candidates’ votes and shares.




Input to asJSON(keep_vec_names=TRUE) is a named vector. In a future version of jsonlite, this option will not be supported, and named vectors will be translated into arrays instead of objects. If you want JSON object output, please use a named list instead. See ?toJSON.
Input to asJSON(keep_vec_names=TRUE) is a named vector. In a future version of jsonlite, this option will not be supported, and named vectors will be translated into arrays instead of objects. If you want JSON object output, please use a named list instead. See ?toJSON.
Input to asJSON(keep_vec_names=TRUE) is a named vector. In a future version of jsonlite, this option will not be supported, and named vectors will be translated into arrays instead of objects. If you want JSON object output, please use a named list instead. See ?toJSON.
Input to asJSON(keep_vec_names=TRUE) is a named vector. In a future version of jsonlite, this option will not be supported, and named vectors will be translated into arrays instead of objects. If you want JSON object output, please use a named list instead. See ?toJSON.







How to read it. Margin is the Democratic candidate’s share minus the Republican candidate’s share, calculated among votes for those two candidates only. A positive margin favors Harris; a negative margin favors Trump. Other candidates are excluded from this two-party comparison.



These are the ten counties where the 2024 Democratic–Republican two-party margin was nearest to zero.







Sources: California Secretary of State, November 5, 2024 Statement of Vote, President by County (XLSX); county boundaries: U.S. Census Bureau, 2024 TIGER/Line County shapefile.





A NOTE ON ELECTION SHIFTS



The county-level 2026 results shown here are for a gubernatorial primary; the historical map is for the 2024 presidential general election. Those are different offices and election types, so comparing their county margins would not measure a meaningful election shift.

title: About
text:
ABOUT THE PROJECT



California Votes: 2026 is a college data science project about understanding election results through thoughtful analysis and accessible visualizations.

title: About
text:
What this site will do
The project will organize verified California election information, describe the methods used to analyze it, and make geographic patterns easier to explore. The goal is to inform—not to predict or imply results before reliable data is available.

title: About
text:
Data and methods
Election results, source citations, and analytical details will be added here alongside the relevant findings. Until then, this site contains no election statistics or outcome claims.
